voyage.name: Piazza del Duomo
voyage.content: An attractive, lively baroque square. Here you can find the Fontana dell'Elefante (Elephant Fountain) or U Liotru - the symbol of the city. There are three buildings here that are World Heritage Sites. The square is also an entrance to the elegant via Etnea, the main shopping street.

voyage.name: Cattedrale di Sant'Agata
voyage.content: An imposing cathedral, well worth visiting. Also see for Terme Achilliane and Museo Diocesano which are located there.

voyage.name: Museo Diocesano
voyage.price: €7; combined ticked incl. museum, Terme Achilliane, Benedictine Monastery €13
voyage.content: The collection of the museum contains various religious artefacts from the Cathedral and some other churches around. Its ticket office also sells tickets to the Terme Achilliane.

voyage.name: Palazzo degli Elefanti
voyage.content: Construction begin in 1696. In 1736 a statue of an elephant carrying an obelisk was erected in front of the palazzo.

voyage.name: Chiesa della Badia di Sant'Agata
voyage.hours: Guided tours to the dome and the terraces: Tue 09:00-12:00, Wed-Sat 09:30 -12:30, 15:30-17:30; Sun 09:30-12:30, 19:00-20:30

voyage.name: Castello Ursino
voyage.content: It was built in the 13th century as a royal castle of the Kingdom of Sicily, and ilater became the seat of the Sicilian Parliament. It hosts the Museo Civico (civic museum), which displays Greek and Roman artifacts from the city; art from the 17th-19th centuries; 2000 bronze figurines from the Archaic, Siceliot, Greek, Etruscan-Italic and Hellenistic eras; and temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: Monastero dei Benedettini di San Nicolò l'Arena
voyage.price: Free entrance to the exterior areas, interor with guided tour €10, which starts daily around 13:00 and hourly during summer. English tours at 13:00 and 16:00
voyage.content: It is the oldest one in Sicily and it is one of the biggest monasteries in Europe. It hosts now the Faculty of Literature of the University of Catania.

voyage.name: Chiesa di San Nicolò l'Arena
voyage.price: Free entrance; visit to the eaves €3
voyage.content: It is an unachieved church which was supposed to be the biggest one in Sicily.

voyage.name: Via Crociferi
voyage.content: It's a centre of an ecclesiastical architecture in Catania: in no more than 200 m there are 4 churches, 3 monasteries and a college.

voyage.name: Monastero di San Benedetto
voyage.content: A splendid baroque monument.

voyage.name: Chiesa di San Francesco Borgia
voyage.content: Today the church used for various cultural events. Next to the church is a former Jesuit college.

voyage.name: Villa Cerami
voyage.content: A Baroque villa. It hosts Faculty of Law of the University.

voyage.name: Palazzo Biscari
voyage.content: It is one of the most interesting baroque palaces in Catania. The palace is privately owned. Check with the tourist office to arrange a visit.

voyage.name: Teatro Romano e Odeon
voyage.content: The theatre dates back to the 1st century CE when it was built on the remains of the Greek theatre it used to hold up to 7000 spectators. Odeon, a smaller theatrical building, was built next to it in the 2nd century CE.

voyage.name: Terme della Rotonda
voyage.content: The remains of ancient Roman baths.

voyage.name: Anfiteatro Romano
voyage.content: Some modest remains amidst the square.

voyage.name: Terme Achilliane
voyage.content: The remains of a small part of a large ancient baths located underground is open for the public. It's under the Catania's Cathedral square. Some parts of mosaics and marble floor as well as some remains of decorated walls. The remains are still quite impressive.

voyage.name: Teatro Massimo Bellini
voyage.content: A 19th-century opera theatre named after the Catania-born composer Vincenzo Bellini. The square before the theatre is a popular meeting place among the local young people, so its neighbourhood is very lively and busy by night.

voyage.name: Palazzo Della Cultura
voyage.alt: ex Convento S.Placido, aka Palazzo Platamone
voyage.content: A former monastery, it's now a venue for various exhibitions. It also hosts the access point, an information office of the municipal museums (M-Sa 09:00-13:00).

voyage.name: Palazzo Gravina-Cruyllas
voyage.content: It is the birthplace of Vincenzo Bellini. Thete are two museums here.

voyage.name: Museo Belliniano
voyage.content: A museum devoted to Vincenzo Bellini, a famous Italian composer.

voyage.name: Museo Emilio Greco
voyage.content: A museum devoted to Italian artist Emilio Greco.

voyage.name: Quattro Canti
voyage.content: A square at the intersection of Via Etnea with Via di Sangiuliano. It is somewhat reminiscent to the other octagonal squares in Italy: Quattro Canti at the piazza Vigliena in Palermo, Quattro Canti in Paternò, and Quattro Fontane in Rome, next to the church of San Carlino by Francesco Borromini.

voyage.name: Porta Garibaldi
voyage.content: The gates erected in 1768 in honor of King Ferdinand IV and his family.

voyage.name: Giardino Bellini
voyage.content: Charming 19th-century park. The oldest part of it, the Prince of Biscari's Maze or Laberinto Biscari, dates back to the 18th century.

voyage.name: Orto Botanico dell'Università di Catania
voyage.content: Small botanical garden of the University of Catania.

voyage.name: Via Etnea
voyage.content: Walk the main shopping avenue, running north from the Piazza del Duomo has most of the city's imposing building and is busy throughout the day and evening. Lots of churches. This road is the equivalent of Las Ramblas in Barcelona, so in the evenings the local people put on their Sunday clothes and walk at a relaxed pace along this avenue.

voyage.name: EtnaWay
voyage.content: Guided excursions on mount Etna, with transfer from Catania, Giarre or Taormina by jeep and 4x4. Visit of summit craters and most beautiful places of the volcano.

voyage.name: Federico II
voyage.alt: School of Italian language and culture
voyage.content: The school is hosted in a Baroque building downtown. The school offers year-round intensive language courses, full immersion classes for all levels, while the afternoon provides a program of cultural activities to learn the culture and practice the language. The cultural themes of the lectures are: cinema, art history, songs and music, traditions and mythology, visits to museums and monuments, food and wine tasting.

voyage.name: Fera 'o Luni
voyage.content: A bustling food and clothes market. The main historic market of Catania.

voyage.name: La Piscaria
voyage.content: A large fish, fruit & veg market just off Piazza Duomo.

voyage.name: Baubò Art Factory
voyage.content: Cute shop run by local artist selling artisanal prints, drawings, and jewellery.

voyage.name: Vetriamo
voyage.content: Stained-glass store with all the products made by the proprietor. Has many suitcase size appropriate pieces, on a variety of local themes.

voyage.name: Camelot
voyage.content: Okay for the meat lover, fish is from frozen.

voyage.name: L'Angolo dello Chef
voyage.content: Humble home cooking joint. Traditional Sicilian dishes from caponata to polli alla brace.

voyage.name: Il Borgo di Federico
voyage.content: A Sicilian restaurant.

voyage.name: Ristorante da Antonio
voyage.content: Italian cuisine

voyage.name: Scirocco Sicilian Fish Lab
voyage.content: Seafood

voyage.name: Dopo Teatro
voyage.content: Panineria with tables. Known for grilled meats.

voyage.name: Del centro
voyage.content: Pizza

voyage.name: Voglia Di Pizza Di Santagati Alfio
Sicilia in Bocca
voyage.content: Typical Sicilian food and pizza. There's another restaurant in town with this name: it's on Piazza Pietro Lupo but it's not recommended. And there's yet another 10 km north up the mountain.

voyage.name: Trattoria Il Mare
voyage.content: Delicious seafood. Casual atmosphere.

voyage.name: Spinella Pasticceria
voyage.content: Sicilian cakes, cannolis, arancini, espresso. Outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Trattoria di Fiore
voyage.content: Classic Sicilian food in a small family trattoria.

voyage.name: Trattoria da Antonio
voyage.content: Reasonably priced fresh seafood.

voyage.name: Al Cavalier Roxy
voyage.content: Sicilian cuisine.

voyage.name: Trattoria U Fucularu
voyage.content: Antipasto buffet, grilled meats.

voyage.name: Grammazita
voyage.content: Bohemian bar with wine, beer, cocktails. Has live music performances most nights, LGBTQ+ friendly. Also has an associated bookshop next door with children's toys and local art prints.

voyage.name: Vermut
voyage.content: Very lively bar with a huge selection of Vermouths (as the name would imply) among other drinks. Lots of young folks in the evenings, so can be hard to find a table.

voyage.name: Retrò
voyage.content: Fancy-ish cocktail bar, with menu of original drinks inspired by famous paintings. Owners happy to talk shop about their craft.

voyage.name: Agora Hostel
voyage.price: Beds in a dorm rooms from €14
voyage.content: In a backstreet under the Duomo, it's lively and can fill up even out of season.

voyage.name: Ananda B&B
voyage.content: B&B in the centre, walking distance from the Bellini Gardens, Via Etnea and the Market.

voyage.name: Suite Inn Catania
voyage.content: Clean & central b&b.

voyage.name: B&B Opera
voyage.content: Central b&b, rooms have balconies, bathroom, hairdryer, TV, air conditioning, minibar. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Hotel Etnea 316
voyage.content: Bright and airy 3-star guest house ideal for young travellers.

voyage.name: Hotel Valentino
voyage.content: Central 3-star hotel with friendly staff and a pleasant and peaceful atmosphere.

voyage.name: BAD: Bed and Breakfast and Design
voyage.content: Simple hostel, striving to be funky.

voyage.name: Hotel Rigel
voyage.content: Clean and comfortable 3-star hotel very near bus station.

voyage.name: Hotel Villa Romeo
voyage.content: Clean, comfortable 3-star hotel very near the railway & bus stations.

voyage.name: B&B Globetrotter Catania
voyage.content: An antique building that has been renovated. B&B (also rents independent apartments) with fully equipped kitchen, bathroom, air conditioning, TV, DVD, HiFi, internet Wi-Fi and hairdryer.

voyage.name: Agriturismo San Leonardello
voyage.address: 165 Via Madonna della Liberta, San Leonardello
voyage.content: Rustic farmhouse off highway close to Etna, Taormina and the beach resorts of Riposto and Acireale.

voyage.name: La Pietra Antica O Munti
voyage.content: Farm accommodation on flanks of Etna.

voyage.name: Agriturismo Arrigo
voyage.content: Farmhouse on flanks of Etna.

voyage.name: Villa Etelka
voyage.content: Villa with sea view and swimming pool.

voyage.name: Hotel Agathae
voyage.content: 3-star accommodation

voyage.name: Gresi Hotel
voyage.content: Clean, AC, bathroom, balcony, high arched ceilings with paintings.

voyage.name: Hotel il Principe
voyage.content: Boutique hotel in a restored aristocratic building, very central near Cathedral.

voyage.name: Hotel La Ville
voyage.content: One of the oldest hotels in Catania, it's a large 3-star family run establishment. Self catering apartments also available.

voyage.name: Hotel Nettuno
voyage.content: Modern 4-star beach hotel with open air swimming pool, restaurants, health spa and meeting facilities. For families and corporate travellers.

voyage.name: Luxury Hotel Romano Palace
voyage.content: Beach resort, very close to airport, with Jacuzzi, private beach and restaurant.

voyage.name: Four Points by Sheraton Catania
voyage.content: Hotel & conference centre with 162 rooms and 7 suites. With sea-water pool and beach access.

voyage.name: Villa Cibele
voyage.content: The hotel is in an elegant early 19th-century building edge of town. Clean & quiet, good if you're touring with your own car.

voyage.name: Eco Hostel
voyage.content: A modern hostel.

voyage.name: Castello di Aci
voyage.content: A medieval castle perched on a giant rock, right over the sea. Contains a small civic museum.
